bounds.domain: Two one-shot calls and two signal owners. Three configurations cover shared signals, separate signals and one signalled/one unsignalled call. Each owner chooses one of four reason instances: native DOMException AbortError, native DOMException TimeoutError, legacy missing reason or an opaque writable custom reason; each owner aborts at most once. Calls have idle, running, settled and done phases.
bounds.atomicity: The first-party adapter registers its once listener, checks pre-abort and invokes the SDK without an await; these operations form one begin step. A native AbortSignal event synchronously forwards to all its active once listeners. SDK promise settlement and the adapter finally continuation are separate. A pre-aborted request still invokes the SDK with an already-aborted owned controller.
bounds.outcomes: The SDK may succeed or fail after a derived abort, including webhook reply or already committed work. The adapter preserves that actual outcome. The abort result denotes rejection with the derived reason and requires a derived abort; an unrelated SDK AbortError is part of generic SDK failure. The model proves no fabricated result, not that every abort prevents an SDK effect or forces a cancellation result.
bounds.reasonIdentity: Native and legacy aborts obtain distinct owned writable reasons for each call. Native AbortError and TimeoutError preserve their original name; legacy missing reasons use AbortError. Custom writable reasons retain the caller's opaque identity and name category, including sharing one custom reason across calls. The adapter preserves caller signal ownership and reason identity/category. External SDK message decoration or SDK-specific error replacement is not represented; the SDK's actual outcome is preserved independently.
bounds.conformance: The maintained service.start-retry integration file checks real SDK clients and loopback HTTP: eleven cancellation cases including shared and separate concurrent signals and a natural request-started native timeout, plus nine existing startup/poller cases. The hook requires all twenty named tests without skips. Source-linked scenarios do not prove refinement for every abstract schedule.
bounds.gaps: The model starts after installation on both owned SDK clients. Middleware wiring, repeated installation, external Context/Composer/TelegramError identity, URL redaction and stack contents, arbitrary custom reason objects or getters, listener API failures, worker-thread or custom non-native signal behavior, SDK internals, HTTP effects, process termination and physical Telegram servers are outside this finite model. Implementation and packed-consumer checks qualify their stated boundaries separately.
